notes: This source/test traceability contract covers the bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 Subscribe Interaction Class service in Umbra's opt-in, non-installable development profile. The declaration transition establishes ordinary interaction delivery eligibility for the invoking federate. Its focused production-filesystem regression adds the successful-void service-report boundary: an invalid class appends nothing, while an accepted passive subscription appends type-27 InteractionClassHandle and type-6 Boolean arguments before any separately queued declaration advisories. The official C++ binding names its Boolean `active`; the standards-facing Optional passive subscription indicator is therefore serialized as its inverse. Section 11.5.1 defines the Boolean text as lowercase `true`/`false`; RL-079 records the divergent uppercase Table 5 example. The Requirements Lab currently assigns this service-level candidate on its coalesced source page to clause-5.10.2; RL-078 records that ownership mismatch while the service/test descriptions retain the direct §5.10 source context. Timestamped interaction behavior, advisory delivery matrices, MOM interaction delivery, save/restore, DDM, remote transport, catalog evidence, validation, and conformance remain outside this slice.
